learn.hook: A river is like a traveller. It is born high in the mountains and walks hundreds of kilometres to meet the sea. Let's follow its path!
points: The place where a river begins is its source. Many Indian rivers begin at a glacier (a huge river of ice) or a spring, high in the mountains.
In the mountains, the river is narrow and flows very fast. It rolls rocks and stones along with it.
In the plains, the river becomes wider and slower. It spreads fine, rich soil called silt on its banks.
Smaller rivers that join a big river are called tributaries. The place where two rivers meet is a confluence (sangam).
The place where a river meets the sea is its mouth. Near the mouth, a river may split into many branches and drop silt to form a delta.

example.q: Why does a river flow fast in the mountains but slowly in the plains?
steps: In the mountains the slope is steep, so water rushes down.
In the plains the land is almost flat, so water moves slowly.
example.answer: The steep slope of the mountains makes it fast; the flat plains make it slow.

learn.reallife: If you visit Rishikesh, you can see the Ganga rushing fast over stones. At Patna or Kolkata, the same river is very wide and calm.

games.title: A river's journey
games.prompt: Put the river's journey in order
items: Source: a glacier high in the mountains
Fast, narrow stream among rocks
Wide, slow river in the plains
Delta with many branches
Mouth: meets the sea

games.title: River words
pairs: Where a river meets the sea
A small river joining a big one
Land made of silt at a river's mouth

quiz.q: The place where a river begins is called its
quiz.explain: A river starts at its source, such as a glacier, a spring or a lake.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the start (source) with the end (mouth)

quiz.q: What is a glacier?
options: A huge, slow-moving mass of ice
quiz.explain: A glacier is a giant river of ice found high in cold mountains. Its melting ice feeds many rivers.
quiz.mistake: Does not know where mountain rivers get their water

quiz.q: Where does a river usually flow the fastest?
options: In the mountains, near its source
quiz.explain: Mountains have steep slopes, so the water rushes down quickly.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a river is fastest where it is widest

quiz.q: A small river that joins a bigger river is called a
quiz.explain: A tributary brings its water into a bigger main river. The Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a joining river with the place where a river ends

quiz.q: The fine, rich soil that a river spreads on its banks is called
quiz.explain: Rivers carry tiny bits of soil called silt. When floods spread it on the land, the soil becomes good for farming.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers carry only sand or stones

quiz.q: The place where a river meets the sea is called its
quiz.explain: A river ends at its mouth, where it pours into a sea or ocean.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the end (mouth) with the beginning (source)

quiz.q: Why do many rivers that start in the Himalayas have water all year round?
options: It rains there every single day
They get water from melting snow and glaciers
quiz.explain: Snow and glaciers melt, especially in summer, so these rivers keep flowing even when there is no rain.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers get water only from rain

quiz.q: Which place is a delta?
options: Land near a river's mouth made of silt, with many branches
quiz.explain: As the river slows near the sea, it drops its silt. Over many years this builds new land called a delta.
quiz.mistake: Does not know a delta forms at the end of the river

teach.ask: Gappu floats on a leaf boat: 'Where does a river start, and where does it end? I want to know the whole trip!'
teach.praise: What a trip! From a glacier in the mountains, through the plains, to the mouth at the sea. My leaf boat is ready!
teach.nudge: Where does the river begin its journey? And where does it finally end?

learn.hook: The Ganga begins as icy water from a glacier and ends in a delta with tigers. India's rivers have amazing stories!
points: The Ganga begins at the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand. There it is called the Bhagirathi. At Devprayag it joins the Alaknanda and is called the Ganga.
The Yamuna begins at the Yamunotri glacier. It joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. Delhi and Agra are on the banks of the Yamuna.
The Brahmaputra begins in Tibet and flows through Arunachal Pradesh and Assam. Majuli, a huge river island, is in the Brahmaputra.
The Ganga and Brahmaputra flow into the Bay of Bengal and together form the Sundarbans delta, home of the Royal Bengal tiger.
The Narmada begins at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows west into the Arabian Sea. The Godavari and Kaveri flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

example.q: Two friends live on the banks of the same river: one in Delhi and one in Agra. Which river is it?
steps: Both Delhi and Agra are in north India.
The Taj Mahal in Agra stands on the bank of the Yamuna.
Delhi is also on the Yamuna.

learn.reallife: Look at an India map: most big rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal, but the Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea.

items.q: Varanasi is on the banks of which river?
Ganga and Yamuna meet at which city?
Which river flows west into the Arabian Sea from Amarkantak?
The Sundarbans delta lies along which sea?
The Taj Mahal is on which river?

quiz.q: The Ganga begins at which glacier?
quiz.explain: The Ganga starts from the Gangotri glacier in Uttarakhand.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the source of the Ganga with that of the Yamuna

quiz.q: At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi joins which river to become the Ganga?
quiz.explain: The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet at Devprayag. From there the river is called the Ganga.
quiz.mistake: Picks a river from south India that is far away

quiz.q: Which river is a tributary of the Ganga and meets it at Prayagraj?
quiz.explain: The Yamuna joins the Ganga at Prayagraj. This meeting point is called the Sangam.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which rivers join the Ganga

quiz.q: Into which sea does the Ganga finally flow?
options: It does not reach any sea
quiz.explain: The Ganga flows east and enters the Bay of Bengal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the east coast and the west coast

quiz.q: Which of these rivers flows west into the Arabian Sea?
quiz.explain: The Narmada flows from Amarkantak towards the west and enters the Arabian Sea in Gujarat.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all big Indian rivers flow east

quiz.q: Majuli, a huge island in the middle of a river, is in which river?
quiz.explain: Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra in Assam.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Assam with the Brahmaputra

quiz.q: Which animal lives in the Sundarbans delta?
quiz.explain: The Sundarbans mangrove forest in the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta is home to the Royal Bengal tiger.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up animals of the delta with animals of mountains, Gir or the desert

quiz.q: Where does the Brahmaputra begin?
quiz.explain: The Brahmaputra starts in Tibet, then enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every river of India begins inside India

teach.ask: Gappu looks at a map: 'Tell me about the Ganga! Where does it begin and where does it end?'
teach.praise: Super! From the Gangotri glacier to the Bay of Bengal, with friends like the Yamuna joining on the way!
teach.nudge: Where does the Ganga start? And where does it meet the sea?

learn.hook: Long ago, people chose to live near rivers. Even today, many of our biggest cities stand on river banks. Can you guess why?
points: Rivers give water for drinking, farming, washing and cattle.
The silt spread by rivers makes the land fertile, so farmers grow rice, wheat and sugarcane in river plains.
Fishermen catch fish, and boats carry people and goods on rivers. Dams on rivers store water and make electricity.
Rivers are home to fish, turtles, crocodiles and the Ganges river dolphin, India's national aquatic animal.
Sewage, factory waste and plastic make rivers dirty. Keeping rivers clean keeps people, animals and plants healthy.

example.q: Many towns in the past grew on river banks. Think it through: why?
steps: The soil near rivers is good for growing food.
Boats on rivers help in travel and trade.
example.answer: Rivers give water, fertile land for food, and a way to travel.

learn.reallife: Varanasi and Patna on the Ganga, Guwahati on the Brahmaputra and Ahmedabad on the Sabarmati are cities that grew beside rivers.

games.title: Helps or harms the river?
items: Throwing plastic in the water
Planting trees on the banks
Letting factory waste flow in
Cleaning the ghats
Dumping garbage on the river bank
Treating sewage before it reaches the river
Using a dustbin at a river picnic

games.title: River life
items: The Ganges river dolphin is India's national aquatic animal.
It was declared India's national aquatic animal in 2009.
Silt from rivers makes farmland less fertile.
Silt adds nutrients and makes the soil more fertile.
Dams can be used to make electricity.
Falling water from a dam turns turbines to make electricity.
Plastic thrown in a river simply disappears.
Plastic does not rot away; it harms fish, turtles and dolphins.
Ahmedabad is on the banks of the Sabarmati.
The Sabarmati river flows through Ahmedabad.

quiz.q: Why is land in river plains good for farming?
options: Rivers spread fertile silt on it
quiz.explain: Silt from rivers is rich in nutrients, so crops grow well in river plains.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that silt makes soil fertile

quiz.q: Which is India's national aquatic animal?
quiz.explain: The Ganges river dolphin was named India's national aquatic animal in 2009. It lives in rivers, not the sea.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a big sea animal instead of a river animal

quiz.q: What can a dam on a river help to do?
quiz.explain: Dams hold back river water for farming and drinking, and the falling water can make electricity.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the uses of dams

quiz.q: Which city stands on the banks of the Brahmaputra?
quiz.explain: Guwahati in Assam is on the Brahmaputra.
quiz.mistake: Picks a city that is not on any big river from that region

quiz.q: Which of these makes a river dirty?
options: Pouring sewage and factory waste into it
quiz.explain: Sewage and factory waste carry dirt and harmful things into the water.
quiz.mistake: Thinks harmless activities pollute a river

quiz.q: Who depends on a river to earn a living by catching fish?
quiz.explain: Fisherfolk catch fish from rivers and sell them.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the job with the river

quiz.q: Ravi sees a plastic bottle floating in the river at a picnic. What is the best thing to do?
options: Jump into the deep water alone to get it
Ask an adult to help pick it out safely and put it in a dustbin
quiz.explain: Plastic harms river animals, but safety comes first: an adult can help remove it safely.
quiz.mistake: Forgets about safety or thinks plastic melts away

quiz.q: Why did many big cities grow along rivers?
options: Rivers gave water, food and an easy way to travel
quiz.explain: Water for drinking and farming, fish to eat and boats for trade made river banks good places to live.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the many uses of rivers

teach.ask: Gappu watches a boat: 'Why do so many people live near rivers? And how can we keep rivers happy?'
teach.praise: Now I see! Rivers give us water, food and travel, so we must keep them clean. I will tell all my bird friends!
teach.nudge: What do rivers give people? And what must we stop throwing into them?
